headline: Software Training Specialist (Clinical) | Client-Facing EHR Training and Go-Live Support | MBBS-Trained Physician
summary: MBBS-trained physician with four years at Greenway Health, a US EHR company, where I implemented close to 200 client practices and trained 200+ end users: providers, nurse practitioners, nurses and medical assistants. I built practice-specific workflows before teaching them, and supported setup through go-live. Before that I ran in-person training for 500+ people as an occupational health physician and 12+ nurses in a COVID ICU. I use Claude and other gen-AI tools for training material, prototypes and the two apps I built myself. My clinical background is acute and outpatient care; I have not worked in skilled nursing.
greenway_bullets: Trained 200+ end users across close to 200 client practices, including providers, nurse practitioners, nurses and medical assistants, in remote sessions.
Ran discovery with each practice to document current workflows, then configured practice-specific workflows and widgets so training matched how the clinic actually works.
Turned recurring training questions and client pain points into feature requests with product teams; many of those features shipped to clients.
Triaged defects and patient safety issues through stage-gate release as a member of the Patient Safety Committee, Functional Advisory Committee and Clinical Content Team.
Presented to clients and at the Greenway Engage provider conference (50 attendees).
Clinical lead for a new AI-first EHR from Aug 2025: provider personas, workflow mapping and React prototypes before engineering handoff.
skills: client-facing EHR training, virtual sessions, in-person group training, role-based curricula, SOP writing, adult learners, conference presentations
clinical workflow discovery, configuration, go-live support, issue triage and escalation, customer communication
ICU, emergency and outpatient workflows; patient safety review; gen-AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini), Claude Code, React, GitHub, n8n
thesis_html: People keep using software when the training looks like their shift.
